newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woolworths sees consumer confidence up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woolworths sees consumer confidence up.

text.p: Woolworth's Ltd, Australia's largest food retailer, said on Monday there were indications of improved consumer confidence in Australia following poor Christmas sales for the retailing industry.
"...We can sense there is a slightly improved level of consumer confidence...", managing director Reg Clairs told reporters.
Woolworths earlier reported an 8.62 percent rise in net profit to A$147.5 million for the 28 weeks ended January 5.

"The flow on effects of the reductions in interest rates will have an impact, slowly, very slowly and progressively," Clairs said. He said he was confident Woolworths, which has just over 34 percent of Australia's grocery market, would maintain sales growth of around the level achieved in the first half.
"I am confident that we will be able to maintain that kind of sales growth we have expressed here over the last few months into the months ahead," Clairs said.
Woolworths reported a 8.61 percent rise in sales to A$8.22 billion in the 1996/97 first half.
"We are reasonably confident we will be able to maintain that growth in all three divisions, in Big W, in the food division and within the speciality division," Clairs said.
Clairs said earlier the rest of the year would be reasonably good for the company in terms of sales and profit. "Our biggest challenge is containing our costs of running the business."
Woolworths reported a flat net profit of A$233.6 million in the 1995/96 year, compared with A$233.5 million a year earlier.
Woolworths shares ended four cents higher at A$3.39.
